Definition: {to advance, i.e. pass on or continue; causatively, to remove; specifically, to bedeck (i.e. bring an ornament upon)}
BiblicalUsage: Ada is the Aramaic verb for passing on, being removed, taken away. "He removeth kings, and setteth up kings"; to Nebuchadnezzar the voice said, "The kingdom is departed from thee"; and of the Son of Man, "his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away." The same verb takes kingdoms away and promises one that will never be taken.
TheologicalSignificance: An Aramaic verb for passing away is a small word, and the contrast in Daniel does the preaching — kingdoms pass, and His dominion does not.
